content.thinking: Alright, I've been iterating through the UI enhancements for the game. So far I've added remote animation handling in `main.js`, fleshed out the HUD with viewmodel sprites, impact sparks, weapon card art, and even upgraded the buy card UI to show artwork. The next logical piece is the map picker UI – it currently just displays the map name and description, but we want it to also show a preview image of each map, similar to how weapon cards now show their art. First, I need to locate where the map cards are generated. Scanning through `app/public/js/main.js`, I recall there being a loop that creates a button element for each map, sets its class, and fills its innerHTML with the name and description. The relevant snippet is: ```js const card = document.createElement('button'); card.className = 'map-card' + (m.id === selectedMap ? ' active' : ''); card.innerHTML = `${m.name}${m.desc}`; ``` This matches the `old_string` I have in my notes. To add a background image, I need to insert a line that sets `card.style.backgroundImage`. I want the same visual treatment as other UI elements: a dark gradient overlay to keep text readable, plus the actual map thumbnail. The gradient used elsewhere (e.g., weapon cards) is `linear-gradient(rgba(7,10,18,0.25), rgba(7,10,18,0.78))`. I'll reuse that. The new line should be: ```js card.style.backgroundImage = `linear-gradient(rgba(7,10,18,0.25), rgba(7,10,18,0.78)), url(assets/maps/${m.id}.png)`; ``` I'll place this right after setting the class name and before assigning `innerHTML`, preserving the original order. The `new_string` will therefore be the three lines: class assignment, the new `style.backgroundImage` line, and the unchanged `innerHTML` line. Now I need to issue an edit command targeting exactly this snippet. Since I only want to replace this specific block and not any other occurrence, `replace_all` should be `false`. The `file_path` is `/home/lane/AIArchives/archives/neonstrike/app/public/js/main.js`. The `old_string` is the three-line snippet as it currently appears, and the `new_string` includes the added style line. Everything lines up, so I’ll execute the edit tool with these parameters.
